confirm.text: These are selections on the air job OWL multi-select, not reported events. Per Kelby Hammer's 09/23 guidance they are reported so the technician can confirm what was meant. Nothing in today's forms describes an actual unsafe condition in narrative, and "Stop work authority utilized" was not selected on any form today — every stop-work item selected was the routine "Stop work authority was discussed".
Forms selecting "Unsafe conditions", with no narrative naming a condition:
Michael Jobe — XTO, Turner W41K 11H, job 35083_1, ended 3:34 PM. Also selected "Stop work authority was discussed". Narrative reads only: "Started the job late but all went well crew was great".

Michael Jobe — XTO, Turner W41J 10H, job 35084_1, ended 3:31 PM. Also selected "Stop work authority was discussed". Narrative reads only: "Had a great meeting went over everything that needed to be done".

William "Jimmy" Cooper 1099 — XTO, Turner W41K 11H, job 35083_2, first of two OWL entries, submitted 2:31 PM. Narrative reads only: "Crews working safely". His second OWL on the same form, 2:37 PM, dropped "Unsafe conditions" and added "Stop work authority was discussed".
Nathan Contreras — XTO, Jack Mohr Unit 3 0124SH, job 35076_1, ended 10:01 AM. See the separate note below.

Michael Jobe selected "Unsafe conditions" on both of his jobs today, which is the second consecutive working day he has done so — he did the same twice on 09/26. That repetition is the training point rather than two separate events.

Nathan Contreras is not the ordinary mis-selection pattern and is worth a direct question. On job 35076_1 he selected "Unsafe conditions" and "Stop work authority was discussed" alongside "Job scope completed safely and as planned", while the same form's Details field reads "Job canceled, arrived at 6:55 a.m and left location at 10:00 a.m". A job recorded as cancelled cannot also have had its scope completed as planned, and no condition is described anywhere on the form. Contreras also appeared on this list on 09/26. Separately, his crew partner Rolando Flores recorded the same job as "Job got rescheduled" rather than cancelled — the two accounts of one job disagree.

Trailer forms of both kinds, and the equipment sections of the H2S Safety Supervision Daily Inspection Form, are photo-based. A defect visible only in a photograph would not surface in this review. In particular, fire extinguisher inspection and expiration dates, first aid kit dates, SCBA and workpack gauge readings, sensor calibration dates and 4-gas calibration dates exist only inside images and not as text, so none of them has been verified here.

One further limitation specific to today: the review window closed at 11:00 PM Central on 09/28, so the usual sweep of the following morning for late-arriving submissions could not be performed. Any form completed on 09/28 but delivered to the mailbox on 09/29 is not counted here, and some of the absences listed above may resolve once this morning's mail is in.
